tools.description: Read a Dendron note's content (frontmatter + body). Callable directly with a governor token. Large notes: pass sections, fields, offset/limit or maxBytes for a bounded read; an unselected read over the byte cap returns a navigable manifest (frontmatter keys and headings) with truncated: true instead of overflowing. TWO DIFFERENT COMPLETENESS FIELDS: truncated means only that the response is not the whole note, so it is true for every selection by construction and answers nothing about your selection; selectionComplete is the field that answers whether what you asked for came back whole. Read selectionComplete — never truncated — before rewriting a field from a slice, because a whole-array write built from a partial read silently destroys the entries you did not see. fieldsNotFound lists any requested field names the note does not carry.

tools.description: Record an ARCH review's findings and receive the computed verdict. The verdict is DERIVED from a frozen finding ledger and a hard round cap, not asserted by the caller: round 1 freezes the ledger, later rounds may only shrink it, and findings first raised after round 1 are returned as deferred rather than blocking. The ledger is bound to the story's CONTENT, not its id — a material amendment to the body, targetFiles or testRequirements rebases it to round 1 with findings blocking again, and the round cap counts rounds per story VERSION. Rebase is derived from a content digest, never requested: there is no parameter that forces or suppresses it. This is the only permitted writer of arch_verdict, arch_round, arch_ledger, arch_deferred, arch_findings_count, arch_subject, arch_total_rounds, arch_round_findings and the arch-approved phase. The phase follows the verdict in BOTH directions: an approved verdict sets phase arch-approved, and a needs-revision verdict on a story at phase arch-approved returns its phase to ready (retraction). A needs-revision verdict never changes any other phase — draft and ready stay as they are, and planned, executing and executed are not demoted. arch_total_rounds and arch_round_findings are ADVISORY: they record cumulative review cost across rebases and never affect the verdict, the cap or the phase. Plan-ready create gate: the handler also runs rks_plan_ready's own create_target_no_authorable_block predicate on the story on every call and refuses approved while any such issue exists; those issues are reported in gateIssues (always present, [] when none), counted in findingsCount, never written to arch_ledger or arch_deferred, and neither the ledger nor the round cap can clear them — only amending the story does. No other plan_ready check affects the verdict.

A +dirty expectation proceeds as anchorMatch dirty-weak — two dirty trees at one HEAD are not the same tree, so it is a weaker guarantee than exact; a +dirty expectation against a clean tree is also dirty-weak, since the expectation itself was stated loosely. The leading @ is optional. If the working-tree anchor cannot be computed at all, the call refuses rather than proceeding unverified.

EITHER WAY the security floor always applies: HTTPS-only, SSRF-guarded (internal/loopback/link-local refused), size-capped + timed out, GET-only, recorded in the write-ledger. Not a crawler; no auth; no JS render.

tools.description: Stage and commit changes. Two modes, exactly one required. Structured mode (message): builds a conventional-commit subject type(scope): message; appends a Co-Authored-By trailer only when coAuthor is supplied. Verbatim mode (rawMessage): commits the complete message (subject, body and trailers) byte-for-byte, with no type(scope) prefix and no trailer added; it requires a non-empty files list and is scoped to those paths only (other staged paths stay staged and uncommitted), cannot be combined with type, scope, message or coAuthor, and returns committedPaths read back from git. reset.description: Force a fresh chain. Re-entering a live session that carries the SAME problemId RESUMES it at its current chain state by default, because discarding a chain silently costs a full refine → plan → exec run. Exception: a story-flow session at 'planned' whose plan is stale against the story (the story content changed since rks_plan was admitted, reason story_changed_since_plan, or its phase no longer admits rks_exec, reason chain_phase_mismatch) is not resumed. Init ends it and returns a NEW token with mode 'stale_reset'; or, when ending it would restore guardrails or pop a pending stash, init returns ok: false with reason 'stale_reset_blocked' and the OLD token still live, and passing reset: true is then the caller's decision. Pass reset: true to start the chain over instead; it ends the old session and returns a NEW token. Needed when re-running a step the current state does not admit — e.g. a QA re-run, whose chain begins at rks_agent_research, which qa_assessing does not allow.

tools.description: ABORT an off-rail session WITHOUT shipping: hard reset to the session's start commit + clean of new untracked files, hooks restored, NO commit, branch, PR, merge, or push. REFUSES rather than discarding when the working tree was ALREADY DIRTY when the session opened — the reset targets a COMMIT, so it would also destroy uncommitted work that predated the session and was never this session's. On refusal it returns ok:false with the pre-existing paths, changes nothing, and leaves the session active; pass discardPreExisting: true to destroy them deliberately. Use this to throw away off-rail work instead of rks_guardrails_on (which always commits/ships). Gitignored paths (node_modules, .env, RAG index) are preserved.

discardPreExisting.description: Explicit opt-in to ALSO discard uncommitted work that already existed when the session opened. Absent or false, such work causes a refusal and nothing is discarded.

EVIDENCE-BOUND: refuses unless a commit reachable from the integration branch carries either the line-exact trailer 'Story: <storyId>' or, for pre-0.66 exec commits, the exact legacy subject line 'feat(exec): <storyId>'. The trailer is preferred when both exist, and the result's evidence.form reports which matched ('trailer' or 'legacy_exec_subject').
